ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU autonomous sanctions, and the Colombian UIAF/Chamber of Commerce PEP databases; enhanced due diligence required for all domestic and foreign PEPs, UBOs, and senior management; continuous transaction monitoring under Superintendencia Financiera Circular Única, Libro I, Título I.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (https://www.rues.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be filed in Spanish using Latin-alphabet characters, including appropriate Spanish accent marks. Non-Latin scripts must be phonetically transliterated into Spanish. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name in the RUES and must comply with Código de Comercio arts. 376-379.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If RUES rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a writ of reconsideration (recurso de reposición) before the same Chamber of Commerce registrar within 10 business days of notification, and simultaneously or subsequently an appellate writ (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the same timeframe. The appellant must attach the RUES search confirmation, a draft of the rejected name, and a stated legal basis. The registry must resolve within 30 business days; if admissible, the name reservation may be extended for one additional 30-day period only if the original reservation has not expired.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a licensed electronic money institution. The S.A.S. must maintain a physical registered office in Colombia with permanent operational personnel, local corporate books, AML/CFT compliance records, and a compliance officer who is subject to on-site supervision by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia. Virtual office addresses are insufficient for the EMI license and may lead to refusal of the special license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 85% risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia within the first 12-18 months after license grant, based on the institution's high-risk AML classification and the supervisory authority's risk-based inspection program.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Colombian S.A.S. Law), particularly Articles 1-5 (constitution through private document), 9 (corporate purpose), 17-19 (capital), 22 (legal representation), 45 (share transfers); complemented by the Colombian Commercial Code (Decreto 410 de 1971) Articles 110, 353-372 (commercial registry), Decree 1074 de 2015 (business formalities), Decree 2555 de 2010 (financial-sector organization) and Ley 1735 de 2014 / Decree 1499 de 2015 (electronic-money institutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) acting as the commercial registry under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism; corporate oversight by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; operating authorization for the electronic-money activity issued by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private constitutive document with notarized signatures) inscribed in the Registro Mercantil; a public deed (Escritura Pública) is only required if real property is contributed. The fintech activity further requires a separate SFC authorization (Autorización de Funcionamiento).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Ley 1258/2008 imposes no minimum paid-up capital; the S.A.S. must only subscribe and pay, in cash or in kind, at least one share under the payment terms fixed in the bylaws. However, as a condition of the e-money license, the SFC requires a fully paid-up regulatory equity of approximately COP 2,000,000,000 (USD ~500,000, as annually adjusted Comisionable), which must be deposited in a blocked escrow-like account at a supervised credit institution and may not be drawn down except as authorized by the SFC during the licensing stage.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDER OF [ENTITY] S.A.S. - WHEREAS the company was lawfully incorporated under Ley 1258 de 2008 and its corporate purpose includes electronic money issuance, virtual IBAN provision and digital wallet reserve management, the sole shareholder unanimously resolves: (1) To ratify the full subscription of all authorized shares and confirm payment of the subscribed capital into the corporate treasury account; (2) To adopt as registered office the address shown in the Chamber of Commerce certificate; (3) To appoint the legal representative, the alternate legal representative and the principal and alternate AML/CFT compliance officers; (4) To instruct the legal representative to file all applications for the fintech license before the Financial Superintendence of Colombia. Unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-validation of the S.A.S. name and availability hold
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the intended domicile, accessed through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) online portal or the Chamber's commercial registry service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a homonymy search application for the proposed corporate name; the Chamber certifies that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trademark or company name; upon approval, request the name reservation certificate and the related hold, which keeps the name available for the statutory term.
required_dossiers: Completed homonymy search form (Formulario de Consulta de Homonimia)
Copy of the national identification (cédula) or passport of each constituent shareholder
Written request identifying up to three alternative corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected for similarity, resubmit with alternative names or file a written rebuttal demonstrating commercial differentiation; the Chamber's denial may be challenged through the 'recurso de reposición' before the same registry within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the constitutive instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría (civil-law notary office) of the registered domicile for signature certification; elevation to a public deed (Escritura Pública) before the same notary where real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the full S.A.S. bylaws: corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose expressly covering electronic money, virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management, capital structure and share classes, governance bodies, legal representative powers and AML/CFT officer assignments; execute the instrument before the notary who certifies the authenticity of signatures and content.
required_dossiers: Draft Documento Privado de Constitución or Escritura Pública matrix
Notarial certification request for signatures and content
Government-issued identification of all shareholders
Notarized power of attorney where a shareholder acts through an attorney-in-fact
Notary KYC/anti-money-laundering information sheet as required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to any clause or identifies omissions, amend the draft and resubmit with the corrected instrument, paying the applicable notarial tariff for the corrected version; the document may be re-executed at the same or another notary without losing its constitutive effects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile - Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed constitutive document together with the Registro Único Empresarial (RUE) form and the pre-RUT; the Chamber verifies the legality of the instrument, the identity of the representatives and the capital subscription, and then enters the company in the Registro Mercantil, issuing the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal after payment of the registration tariff.
required_dossiers: Executed Documento Privado de Constitución or first copy of the notarial deed
RUE registration form (Formulario Único Empresarial)
Pre-RUT issued by DIAN
Statement of capital subscription and payment status
Utility bill or lease agreement evidencing the registered office address
Payment receipt of the commercial registration tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a defect notice (requerimiento), cure the defect within the granted term, generally ten business days, by filing a corrective private document (documento de corrección) executed by all shareholders; if registration is denied twice, apply for the 'saneamiento de la inscripción' procedure or request an order directly from the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fiscal registration before DIAN - NIT and RUT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - online through the official electronic services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) electronically or at a DIAN service point; DIAN assigns the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT), classifies the taxpayer regime and records the economic activity codes corresponding to ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522110; thereafter register the company as an employer before the social security system (PILA) and for the municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) at the local mayor's office.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued by the Chamber
Pre-RUT printout with proposed tax and activity codes
Lease agreement or ownership certificate and address authorization for the registered office
Identification of the legal representative
Bank certificate confirming the corporate account and capital deposits where activated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the tax domicile or the proposed economic codes, file an online RUT correction (aclaración y corrección) with supporting evidence; if the NIT is blocked, present a written request to the competent DIAN regional office attaching the Chamber certificate; adverse determinations may be appealed through the 'recurso de reconsideración.'

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate account and deposit of the regulatory capital reserve
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supervised credit institution (commercial bank) operating in Colombia under SFC supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account in the name of the S.A.S. after completing the bank's KYC and AML/CFT checks; deposit the fully paid-up regulatory equity of approximately COP 2.0 billion into a blocked sub-account or escrow arrangement; obtain the bank's certificate of blocked deposit for use in the SFC application; update the share ledger to evidence the full payment of the subscribed capital.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
NIT and RUT certificates
Extract of the incorporation document showing corporate purpose and capital clauses
Board resolution appointing bank signatories and officers
AML/KYC forms for all shareholders and legal representatives
Source-of-funds declaration (declaración de origen de fondos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account because of the high-risk fintech activity, apply to another supervised credit institution or escalate the matter through the SFC Customer Service Ombudsman; if the blocked-deposit certificate does not reflect the required amount, correct the deficiency by additional deposit or obtain the bank's written confirmation of the escrow terms before filing with the SFC.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Directorate of Taxes and Customs of Colombia (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales – DIAN); electronic channel: MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) available at www.dian.gov.co and muisca.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Colombian S.A.S.: (1) the by-laws are executed before a notary and registered with the Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce), which assigns a provisional 10-digit NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through the single business registry RUES; (2) the legal representative must complete and validate the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with DIAN within the statutory term, either remotely via MUISCA using a qualified digital signature (firma electrónica issued by an accredited certification authority) or in-person at a DIAN service point, declaring IVA-responsible status, withholding-agent status and, when applicable, exporter-of-services status; (3) DIAN then activates the definitive NIT and the entity obtains its electronic invoicing authorization (rango de numeración). For a foreign non-resident entity without Colombian incorporation, the company obtains a corporate NIT by appointing a local attorney-in-fact with public power, filing apostilled constitutional documents, and completing the MUISCA pre-registration followed by in-person validation; however, in this dossier the local operating entity is a Colombian S.A.S. and therefore follows steps (1)-(3). As a mandatory condition precedent, the electronic money institution must first obtain a license from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) as a Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPE) under Decree 2555/2010, and the RUT must accurately reflect ISIC/CIUU Rev.4 class 6619 (auxiliary activities to financial services) together with the SEDPE authorization reference.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a Colombian S.A.S. is an autonomous taxpayer of the Colombian corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta y Complementarios) at the flat 35% statutory rate applicable for FY2024-2025 (Ley 2277/2022); no partnership pass-through or fiscal consolidation is permitted for an S.A.S.; Colombian resident entities are taxed on worldwide income with a foreign tax credit, not on a pure territorial basis; dividends paid to non-resident shareholders attract a 10% final withholding on the after-CIT distributable profit (Art. 408 E.T.), while any untaxed or exempt profit component of the distribution is subject to an additional deemed 35% charge at shareholder level, producing a combined effective rate of approximately 41.5% on fully distributed profits; the optional SIMPLE combined tax regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación) is capped at 80,000 UVT of annual gross income (approx. COP 3.45 billion for FY2024) and is not available to SFC-supervised financial entities such as a licensed EMI/SEDPE; therefore the S.A.S. remains mandatorily within the ordinary entity-level tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no US-style check-the-box or elective pass-through regime; relevant elections and formal mechanisms available to this entity include: (a) ordinary CIT versus the SIMPLE regime, which is generally unavailable to licensed SEDPE financial entities; (b) RUT classification as IVA-responsible with mandatory electronic invoicing, versus the non-resident supplier withholding treatment for foreign providers without a Colombian establishment; (c) the formal election/registration of zero-rated export-of-services status under Art. 481 E.T. for virtual IBAN, digital wallet management and payment processing services supplied exclusively abroad, triggered by updating the RUT as exporter and registering the export operations; (d) transfer pricing and advance-pricing agreements (APA) as voluntary procedural instruments, not substantive tax elections; and (e) hybrid mismatch rules introduced under Ley 2277/2022 which apply automatically without elective carve-outs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre las Ventas – IVA) regulated by the Estatuto Tributario and Decreto Único Reglamentario 1625/2016; complemented by the Financial Transactions Tax (Gravamen a los Movimientos Financieros – GMF) at 4×1000 (0.4%) levied on debit transactions from current and savings account operations of the EMI, and by the ICA municipal industry and commerce tax which is a local levy outside the national indirect tax framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero economic threshold for legal entities: every S.A.S. carrying out taxable supplies must register and remain registered in the RUT as an IVA-responsible taxpayer before commencing operations; the reduced small-trader exemption (natural persons with prior-year gross income not exceeding 3,500 UVT, approximately COP 151 million for FY2024) is not available to companies or to licensed financial entities; accordingly, registration is mandatory regardless of turnover, and no statutory de-minimis relief exists for the Colombian operating entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing under DIAN Resolution 000165/2023: every sales invoice must be issued as a Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV), generated in XML/CII format, digitally signed with an X.509 certificate, transmitted through DIAN web-service APIs (SOAP/REST over HTTPS) or via an authorized Operador Tecnológico/FE (OFE), validated by DIAN before the transaction is fiscally complete, and stamped with the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) or CUDE code plus QR; invoice consecutive numbering must be pre-authorized by DIAN through the rango de numeración mechanism; supporting documents include the Documento Soporte en Adquisiciones a No Obligados and electronic withholding certificates, and the annual exógena information return must be filed with DIAN; in addition, the entity remains subject to SFC information-reporting obligations over its licensed payment rails.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Art. 481 E.T. For the fintech/EMI scope (virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet reserve management, payment and clearing services to non-residents), zero-rating is available only if all of the following criteria are met: (i) the service beneficiary is a person without residence or domicile in Colombia and without a permanent establishment in the country; (ii) the service is rendered from Colombia but utilized exclusively abroad; (iii) the service falls within the exportable-services catalogue of Decreto 1625/2016 (Chapter 1.3.1.9, integrating former Decree 1805/2010), which expressly includes financial, payment, IT and back-office services provided to foreign principals; (iv) the consideration is paid by the non-resident in foreign currency and is channelled through the Colombian exchange market (Mercado Cambiario); and (v) the exporter is registered in the RUT with active exporter status, holds the SEDPE license, and evidences each transaction with the corresponding service export certificate. Domestic financial intermediation income in Colombia is excluded from IVA (without creditable input VAT), so the zero-rating route is the principal mechanism for recovering input VAT embedded in technology, KYC/AML and international office infrastructure; the exporter may offset or obtain a monthly refund of such input VAT in the VAT return, subject to DIAN's refund certification procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX/DAE) and commercial export invoice (factura comercial / Factura Electrónica de Exportación) – mandatory for goods; for pure services, replaced by the DIAN-validated electronic invoice and the signed service export contract

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or equivalent dispatch evidence – applicable to physical goods only; for services, the service delivery log, system usage records and a certificate from the foreign beneficiary confirming exclusive use abroad

Inward Remittance Certificate – Colombian Declaración de Cambio por exportación de servicios lodged through the authorized intermediary of the Mercado Cambiario, evidencing collection of the foreign currency export proceeds within the legal term
RUT excerpt showing active IVA-responsible status, exporter annotation, SEDPE license reference and ISIC/CIUU 6619 registered activity

Certificado de Exportación de Servicios issued through the VUCE single foreign-trade window (when the transaction value exceeds the applicable DIAN threshold) or written registration of the service export transaction with the competent authority
Payment evidence: SWIFT/MT103 credit notices, bank asset cards and reconciliation statements matching the exchange-market declaration with the invoiced amount
E-invoicing transmission receipts (XML, CUFE/CUDE validation codes and DIAN acceptance responses) for each export invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a priority audit area for DIAN. Consequences of non-compliance include: (a) retroactive re-characterization of the 0% rate to 19% IVA on the entire value of the supplies, together with a demand for the tax differential; (b) the Art. 648 inexactness penalty (sanción por inexactitud) of 100% of the understated tax (50% where the difference is minor and not deliberately hidden, and 160% where the claim is supported by false or non-existent invoices); (c) statutory refund-improperness penalties of up to 100% of the value of refunds improperly requested or obtained; (d) monthly default interest at approximately 2.12% per month (circa 28.6% annual) accrued from the original filing date; (e) fines under the Banco de la República exchange-control regime for late, inaccurate or absent Declaración de Cambio and for failure to surrender export proceeds within the 180-day term; (f) criminal liability for fraudulently obtaining tax refunds and offsets (Ley 1762/2015, Código Penal Art. 402) punishable by 7 to 12 years of imprisonment; and (g) administrative measures such as inclusion in DIAN's refund-risk blacklist, pre-audit withholding of refund payments, and suspension of the exporter status. The ordinary DIAN assessment period is 5 years, extended to 10 years where returns are not filed or are based on fraudulent or fictitious documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), exercising foreign-exchange administration jointly with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit under Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015 and the regulatory circulars of the foreign-exchange regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains full convertibility for current-account transactions (trade, services, transfers), but all settlements between residents and non-residents must be routed through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries and recorded on an exchange declaration. Capital-account transactions are freely transferable but require registration with Banco de la República for outbound remittance rights; foreign direct investment into an S.A.S. must be registered to secure future dividend repatriation and capital reduction proceeds. Profit remittance is lawful after tax withholding/clearance, dividend taxation and, for profits attributable to a permanent establishment, remittance tax; repatriation must be done via the authorized FX market with proper supporting declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds are not 'surrendered' to the Central Bank; they are subject to a channeling obligation through the foreign-exchange market. For goods exports, receipts generally must be credited to a Colombian bank account and reported on an exchange declaration within the statutory period (commonly up to six months from export customs declaration, with shorter windows for services). There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into Colombian pesos; the exporter may maintain foreign currency in a local deposit/compensation account, provided the exchange declaration is timely filed and the underlying export is properly registered.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low standalone viability. An offshore digital electronic-money institution cannot issue payment/e-money accounts to Colombian residents, provide virtual IBANs, or hold customer float without a license from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC). It may only operate as a software/processing vendor to an authorized Colombian payment institution or licensed bank. The Colombian legal vehicle for e-money/payments is the SEDPE under Law 1735 of 2014, and non-bank EMIs must partner with supervised banks to access clearing rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote corporate onboarding is rarely permitted. Colombian AML rules under the SFC require identification and risk-profiling of directors and beneficial owners; tier-1 banks typically require the local legal representative and at least one signer to attend an interview in person, while other directors may be verified by notarized documents and controlled videoconference. In practice, a physical presence in Bogotá is the strongest onboarding path; overseas directors must submit apostilled powers and certified identity/source-of-funds records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business model: issuance of virtual IBANs and electronic-money wallet reserve management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SFC license or SEDPE authorization, AML/ATF compliance manual, sanctions screening procedure, transaction-monitoring system description, independent audit opinion, board risk appetite statement and entity risk-rating matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent ownership chain or offshore ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, company register excerpt, detailed shareholding chart up to natural persons, UBO declaration, passports of directors and shareholders, proof of source of wealth and source of funds, and, if a corporate shareholder, its own legal and ownership documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-touch high-value cross-border flows expected in a new fintech treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-month transaction forecast, projected volumes and corridors, merchant/issuer due-diligence policy, counterparty whitelist, payment-purpose classification, geolocation and jurisdiction screening controls, and a written explanation of travel/exposure limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dependence on foreign sponsor banks or offshore EMI infrastructure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Program-management agreement, sponsor bank licence confirmation, host-to-host connectivity diagram, evidence of consolidated compliance ownership, audit access rights, mechanism for local records retention and data-protection compliance under Colombian law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions should be remitted by the non-resident investor via SWIFT MT103 to the S.A.S.'s local bank account, with payment narrative identifying the company NIT, investor entity, invoice/counterparty reference and the purpose code for foreign direct investment (capital contribution). The local bank will file the corresponding exchange declaration with Banco de la República; after funds are received, the SAS must complete the FDI registration (if not already registered) to legally support future dividend remittances and capital repatriation. Funds cannot enter the e-money float and must be credited only to the capital/operational reserve account specified at onboarding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border disbursements and local high-value clearing in Colombian pesos for domestic disbursements. For procurement of goods or large contractual services, an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit opened by the Colombian tier-1 bank is preferred, using the standard SWIFT MT700/MT710 mechanism and settlement at sight or by term draft. Supporting documents (invoice, transport evidence, service certificate) and the applicable import/exchange declaration must be presented, and the bank will apply withholding, VAT and foreign-exchange controls on the disbursement before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD deliverable FX forward contracts with authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediaries
COP/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with investment-grade counterparties for hedging non-convertible/liquidity-constrained positions
COP/USD cross-currency interest-rate swaps to align asset-liability currency profiles
Vanilla COP/USD FX option collars traded with authorized local banking counterparties
FX swaps for short-term liquidity repositioning between COP operational accounts and USD correspondent accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Commercial Registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a fine of up to one monthly legal minimum wage (COP 1,300,000) plus interest; failure for three consecutive years results in administrative strike-off of the commercial registration and loss of corporate validity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Deposit (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval by the shareholders' meeting, but no later than May 31 of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-deposit is subject to monetary fines imposed by the Superintendence of Companies (SuperSociedades) and may lead to the institution being declared inactive or subject to judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income and Complementary Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between August and September of the following taxable year, according to the last two digits of the NIT set annually by DIAN Resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty equivalent to 5% of income tax owed for each month of delay, up to 100% of the unpaid tax; non-filing triggers DIAN's administrative assessment and may lead to the enforceability of sanctions including business registration restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry Update (Registro de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due within one month after the filing of the income tax return, or whenever a shareholding transfer occurs, in accordance with DIAN Resolution 000078/2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the beneficial ownership registry triggers monetary penalties of up to COP 1,000,000 per infraction and administrative enforcement actions, including impediments on corporate transactions and foreign remittances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit and Revisor Fiscal are required for all entities licensed as electronic money institutions under the supervision of the Financial Superintendence of Colombia, irrespective of size; for non-licensed S.A.S. entities, audit is mandatory if total assets exceed 5,000 monthly minimum legal wages, gross income exceeds 3,000 monthly minimum legal wages, or workforce exceeds 200 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP (Normas de Contabilidad y de Información Financiera – NCIF) fully converged with IFRS as issued by the IASB, applicable to financial institutions supervised by the Financial Superintendence.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must maintain a permanent official record of direct and indirect ownership. Any share transfer that results in a change of ultimate beneficial owner must be reported to the Colombian Beneficial Owner Registry (RBF) within one month of the transaction. The annual RBF confirmation must verify all current beneficial owners and reflect transfers exceeding 20% of share capital. Failure to update incorrect or incomplete ownership data is sanctionable by DIAN and may invalidate creditor rights against undisclosed principals.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (plus 3-percentage-point surcharge for credit institutions/financial establishments, yielding 38% for applicable EMIs) [for FY 2024-2025]
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general CIT holiday for S.A.S. fintech/EMI; available benefits: 50% deduction for investments in science, technology and innovation (CTi); foreign-source dividends exemption (95%) available only under the Colombian Holding Company (CHC) regime for qualifying S.A.S.; VAT exemption on digital wallet basic services if properly characterized; net equity taxes: applicable wealth tax surcharge under Law 2277/2022.
